content.text:
Confirmed: commit 2fcabce (parent of the fix, made 10 minutes earlier by the same author) introduced the `HIGH_SCORES_FILENAME` constant with type `int` instead of `String` as part of a larger refactor extracting magic values into named constants.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 2fcabce11d5df9bffc04c639bf24ed8f96c57990

## Reasoning
(1) I traced the history of `TetrisPanel.java` with `git log --follow -p` and `git log -S"HIGH_SCORES_FILENAME"` to find where the constant was first declared and where its type mismatched its usage.

(2) Commit `2fcabce` refactors several previously inline magic literals (window size, delay, colors, filenames) into named `static final` constants. In doing so it declared:
```java
private static final int HIGH_SCORES_FILENAME = "TetrisHighScores.txt";
```
using `int` instead of `String`, while simultaneously replacing the inline literal `"TetrisHighScores.txt"` in the `Scanner`/`FileWriter` calls with this new constant. This is a copy-paste/typo error made while mechanically converting many literals to constants in the same commit (note the adjacent correctly-typed `SCORE_INCREMENT_VALUE` and `MAX_HIGH_SCORES` as `int`, and `MUSIC_FILE`/`TEXT_COLOR` as other types — `HIGH_SCORES_FILENAME` was simply mistyped as `int`).

(3) The very next commit by the same author, 10 minutes later (`8f6274a`), is a single-line fix changing exactly `int` → `String` for this declaration, with no other changes — strongly indicating it's a direct correction of the typo introduced in `2fcabce`. Since a `String` literal assigned to an `int` field is a compile-time type error in Java, the code in `2fcabce` would not have compiled, making this an unambiguous, high-confidence identification of the bug-introducing commit.
